module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Spectrum
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
public import FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Spectrum

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
/--
Lovász Theta Function (ϑ(G))
The Lovász theta function is defined as:
ϑ(G) = min λ_max(A)
where the minimum is taken over all symmetric matrices A such that:

A_ij = 1 for all i = j (diagonal entries are 1)
A_ij = 0 for all {i,j} ∈ E (entries corresponding to edges are 0)
A is positive semidefinite

Here λ_max(A) denotes the maximum eigenvalue of A.
-/
noncomputable def lovaszThetaFunction
    (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℝ :=
  sInf {(Matrix.IsHermitian.maxEigenvalue hA) | (A : Matrix α α ℝ) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
      (_ : ∀ i, A i i = 1) (_ : ∀ i j, G.Adj i j → A i j = 0)}

end SimpleGraph

findings.description: The matrix constraints at lines 41–42 make this function equal to 1 for every nonempty finite graph, rather than the Lovász theta number. The identity matrix satisfies both `∀ i, A i i = 1` and `∀ i j, G.Adj i j → A i j = 0`, so the infimum is at most 1. Conversely, every feasible n×n Hermitian matrix has trace n, hence its largest eigenvalue is at least 1. I proved this constant-value result in Lean. In particular, `(⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).lovaszThetaFunction = 1`, whereas the standard theta number of this edgeless graph is 2. This is not an equivalent characterization or a graph-complement convention.
findings.source_evidence: Donald E. Knuth, “The Sandwich Theorem,” Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 1 (1994), A1, https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/9312214: equation (4.2) specializes the weighted definition to weights identically 1; equations (6.1)–(6.3) minimize the largest eigenvalue of a real symmetric matrix with diagonal entries 1 and entries 1 on nonadjacent pairs, explicitly leaving the other entries unconstrained; equation (12.1) proves equivalence to theta. Equation (4.6) gives θ(K̄_n)=n. Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lov%C3%A1sz_number, “Equivalent expressions” and “Value for well-known graphs,” states the same characterization and edgeless-graph value.
findings.suggested_fix:
Use the standard minimum-largest-eigenvalue characterization:
```
sInf {(Matrix.IsHermitian.maxEigenvalue hA) |
  (A : Matrix α α ℝ) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (_ : ∀ i j, i = j ∨ ¬ G.Adj i j → A i j = 1)}
```
Thus diagonal and nonedge entries are 1, while edge entries are free. Update the docstring accordingly and remove its positive-semidefinite requirement, which is not part of this minimum characterization. Merely adding `A.PosSemidef` to the current constraints would still give the constant value 1.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lov%C3%A1sz_number — definition, equivalent expressions, graph values, properties, and references.
Donald E. Knuth, “The Sandwich Theorem,” Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 1 (1994), A1; TeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/9312214 — notation and sections 1, 3–7, and 12.
https://mathworld.wolfram.com/LovaszNumber.html — definition discussion and graph-values table; the finding is grounded in Knuth and Wikipedia.

No corresponding theta definition was found in Mathlib. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles and proves the constant-value result for all nonempty finite graphs, value 0 for an empty vertex type, the standard formulation's value 2 on the two-vertex edgeless graph, and direct inequivalence. The docstring's unimplemented PSD condition is not a separate numerical defect: adding it to the current minimization still gives 1. No repository files were edited.

Updated the docstring and removed its incorrect positive-semidefinite requirement. The required compile command reports no errors or warnings; a sandboxed Lean regression test proves the corrected value is 2 for the edgeless two-vertex graph.

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Spectrum
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
public import FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Spectrum

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
/--
Lovász Theta Function (ϑ(G))
The Lovász theta function is defined as:
ϑ(G) = min λ_max(A)
where the minimum is taken over all symmetric matrices A such that:

A_ij = 1 whenever i = j or vertices i and j are not adjacent in G.
Entries corresponding to edges are unconstrained.

Here λ_max(A) denotes the maximum eigenvalue of A.
-/
noncomputable def lovaszThetaFunction
    (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℝ :=
  sInf {(Matrix.IsHermitian.maxEigenvalue hA) | (A : Matrix α α ℝ) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
      (_ : ∀ i j, i = j ∨ ¬ G.Adj i j → A i j = 1)}

end SimpleGraph
